inferior spikelets are characterized by a lower level of miRNAs and a lower level of hormones, resulting in poor grain-filling and development.
the inferior spikelets may have a delayed flowering time and a reduced expression of miRNAs during the early stage, resulting in a slower grain-filing rate and an under-developed grain weight.

inferior spikelets are not inferior in terms of grain-filling ability but rather inferior in the sense that the grain-filling ability is suppressed by the inferior environment and/or the differential expression of miRNAs in rice.

the inferior spikelets may be defined to be those where the grain filling is slower due to the lower expression of miRNA cohorts that are involved in multiple developmental and hormone signaling pathways, which consequently lead to a lower grain weight.

the differential expression of miRNAs in the superior and inferior spikelet cohorts may be responsible for the observed differences of grain-filling rate during the early stage, which is consistent with the concept that the inferior spikelets have a slower grain-filing rate than the superior ones.
the inferior spikelets may be the outcome of a series of developmental and signaling events that are differentially expressed in the inferior spikelets and are regulated by miRNAs.

miRNAs play important roles in the development of inferior spikelets and may be a new target for improving the grain-filling rate in inferior spikelets.
